name: NCW Mayhem, 12 March 1997

matches.note: disqualification, after Nelson's manager "Luscious" Linda Lyon struck Tyler with a stiletto heel

notes: The earliest surviving card of NCW's 1997 relaunch (the announced 10 March debut is not in the held record). Opens with an on-air angle in which the Jammer, as interim Commissioner, fines the Trooper for an attack on a referee and defends the stoppage of a prior match; Marcus Magus then talks his way into naming himself the new Commissioner.

name: NCW Mayhem, 18 March 1997

matches.note: pinfall, the Destructive Duo (Jammer & TNT) def. by Mist & the Golem, managed by Mike Surimoko

notes: The card that announces NCW's own four-title structure: JammerWolf Productions' own General Manager, Lucas Garou, reveals the World Heavyweight, Light-Heavyweight-less, Women's, Internet and Tag Team belts will be filled by a series of Free-for-All matches at a first supercard that June. Not itself a title match.

name: NCW Free-for-All

date.source: the fed's own recap posts, dated 16 June 1997 and datelined to the 9 June 1997 event

matches.stipulation: World Internet Championship Free-for-All: a ten-entrant gauntlet, field and entry order drawn at random
matches.note: Crowns the inaugural NCW World Internet Champion. Confirmed entrants from the served text: "Hitman for Hire" Jason Stone (ambushed before he could enter, counted out), Thomas N. Tyler, "L-Train" LaShawn Marcus (eliminated by Tyler's Pain Explosion), the Golem, ... "Flashy" Freddie Massey (eliminated last). "Violent" Victor Frost wins with a powerslam on Massey. The full ten-entrant order is not structured; the served page carries it in full.
Commissioner's Match; Justice becomes NCW's second Commissioner

matches.stipulation: World Women's Championship Free-for-All: a ten-entrant gauntlet, field and entry order drawn at random
matches.note: Crowns the inaugural NCW World Women's Champion. Lupa eliminates Monique Devereaux with a top-rope splash to win; the rest of the ten-entrant field is not structured.

matches.stipulation: World Tag Team Championship Free-for-All: a five-team gauntlet
matches.note: Bad Company (Massey & Venom) win the inaugural NCW World Tag Team Championship, Venom powerbombing the Sinister Squad's Victor Frost for the pin; the beaten Sinister Squad (Frost & Karl Kruger) then hand the belts to Bad Company a second time over, themselves, in an on-air sportsmanship angle. The other three entrant teams are not structured.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Free-for-All: a ten-entrant gauntlet, field and entry order drawn at random
matches.note: Crowns the inaugural NCW World Heavyweight Champion. "The King of Desire" Ray Kinge eliminates the Trooper with a crucifix powerbomb to win; the rest of the ten-entrant field is not structured.

notes: NCW's own founding supercard, a free outdoor show at the Iowa City Pedestrian Mall that crowned all four of the fed's inaugural champions on the same night. Served from the fed's own five-part recap (Countdown, parts 1-3, and a conclusion), all posted 16 June 1997 and folded here into a single show record. Several undercard matches described in the served text (a Chi-Town Rumble, a Falls Count Anywhere brawl, a six-person cage match, and others) are not structured into this record; they are narrated in the served page's own verbatim text.

name: NCW Mayhem, 23 June 1997

date.source: the card's own subject line, [NCW] 6/23/97 from Russia

matches.note: Original Sin (back brain kick) after a slingshot into the ringpost

notes: The European Tour's opening card, framed on air as the start of a westward trek to NCW Overseas at Wembley Stadium that Labor Day -- the held record's single largest capture gap. Commissioner Justice announces Dixie Hart's standing ringside security post. Closes with Eve and Lupa brawling to a stalemate as time runs out.

name: NCW Mayhem, 3 July 1997

matches.note: Bad Company retain the World Tag Team Championship on the tour's first defence

notes: The European Tour's first title defence. Opens on a backstage introduction of the newly-arrived Deathstalkers, the Lord of Darkness among them, with their manager the Devastator.

name: NCW Mayhem, 4 July 1997

matches.note: top-rope splash retains the World Women's Championship

notes: A second title defence on the same tour leg: "Violent" Victor Frost also retains the World Internet Championship, over eXtasy, narrated in the served text but not structured (eXtasy is not minted). Marcus Magus, having lost the Commissioner's office, works to recruit "L-Train" LaShawn Marcus away from Street Level -- the season's own heel-turn arc taking shape.

name: NCW Mayhem, 26 September 1997

matches.note: Double count-out after run-ins from both corners; Eve retains the World Women's Championship (Gauntlet, week 1)
World Internet Championship; the Lord of Darkness retains by disqualification after "Dashing" Derek Lankford's interference
the Sinister Squad win the World Tag Team Championship; Venom was left groggy by Lankford's earlier interference

notes: Three of the fed's own four inaugural title lineages advance on one card, back home in Iowa City after the European Tour. "Dashing" Derek Lankford's interference in the Internet title match sets up the tag title change moments later.

name: NCW Main Event, 3 October 1997

date.source: the card's own dateline, "10-3-97," in a delayed posting (msg_id eAqiiQS4gAgJ)

matches.note: Izcleta wins the World Internet Championship by disqualification, via the Lankford Leglock (standing Figure Four) after "Dashing" Derek Lankford's interference

notes: The last NCW card in the held record: no further editions survive before the fed's silent stop and its 25 November closure. A tag match (the Jammer & Lupa vs. Marcus Magus & "The Doctor" Jim Masters, double count-out) and the Women's Gauntlet's second defence (Eve over Jana, Mistress of Spiders) are narrated in the served text but not structured; Masters and Jana are not minted.
